headline: Possible illness brewing
reason: with resting HR and breathing rate both up
action: Make today a rest day and drink plenty
title: Possible illness brewing
body: Resting heart rate and breathing rate are both well above your normal — the classic early pattern of a cold, infection or overreaching. Make today a rest day, drink plenty, and see how tomorrow's numbers look before training hard.

headline: Resting HR and glucose both up
action: Follow your sick-day rules — keep basal going, check ketones if high
title: Raised heart rate and higher glucose
body: Resting HR is up and glucose has averaged {dx_mean_24h:1} mmol/L over 24h — together that often means illness. Follow your sick-day rules: keep basal insulin going, check ketones if you're running high, drink plenty, and rest.

headline: Wrist temperature up {wrist_temp:1}°C
action: Keep training easy and watch for symptoms
title: Wrist temperature up {wrist_temp:1}°C
body: A raised overnight temperature is often the first sign of illness — it can also follow alcohol, a late heavy meal or a hot room. Keep training easy today and watch for symptoms.

headline: Low: {dx_bg:1} mmol/L
action: Treat it now per your hypo plan and recheck in 15 min
title: Low: {dx_bg:1} mmol/L
body: Treat it now per your hypo plan (typically 15g fast-acting carbs) and recheck in 15 minutes. Don't exercise until you're back above 5.

headline: Glucose dropping ({dx_bg:1})
action: Have fast carbs to hand
title: Dropping: {dx_bg:1} and falling
body: Falling {dx_trend5:1} mmol/L every 5 minutes. Have fast carbs to hand and check the forecast on the Diabetes tab.

headline: High: {dx_bg:1} mmol/L
action: Drink water and check the Diabetes tab
title: High: {dx_bg:1} mmol/L
body: Drink water and check the correction card on the Diabetes tab. If it's been high for a couple of hours or you feel unwell, check ketones.

action: Check the pre-workout advisor before training
title: Training soon? Check first
body: Glucose {dx_bg:1} with {dx_iob:1}u of insulin still active — exercise now could pull you low. Use the pre-workout advisor on the Diabetes tab before you start.

action: Check your sensor and uploader
title: No glucose reading for {dx_bg_age_min} min
body: Check your sensor and the Nightscout uploader — the forecast and alerts can't help while readings are missing.

action: Check Patterns on the Diabetes tab
title: {dx_vlow_7d:1}% of the week under 3.0
body: The consensus target is under 1% below 3.0 mmol/L. Check Patterns on the Diabetes tab for when they happen — repeated serious lows are worth raising with your diabetes team.

action: Check Patterns before your next similar meal or session
title: {dx_hypos_24h} lows in the last 24 hours
body: More than one low in a day usually has a common cause — a meal ratio or basal rate that's too strong, or extra activity. Look at the Diabetes tab's Patterns before your next similar meal or session.

action: Check the overnight part of Patterns
title: Low overnight (down to {dx_night_low:1})
body: Night-time lows disturb sleep and often show up as a poor sleep score and low Body Battery. Late exercise and evening corrections are common causes — check the overnight part of Patterns.

title: Time below range {dx_below_7d:1}% this week
body: The target is under 4% below 3.9 mmol/L. Reducing lows comes before chasing time in range — the Diabetes tab's regimen review shows which time of day needs attention.

reason: with lows alongside lots of training
title: Lows alongside lots of training
body: Exercise raises insulin sensitivity for up to 24-48 hours, so busy training weeks often bring more lows — especially overnight. The workout profiles on the Diabetes tab show how each session type affects you.

title: High overnight (average {dx_night_mean:1})
body: Common causes: a late or high-fat/protein meal (slow, delayed rise), a missed bolus, or basal that's too light overnight. If it repeats, check the overnight window in Patterns.

title: Time in range {dx_tir_7d}% this week
body: Target is 70%+ in 3.9-10 mmol/L. {dx_above_7d}% was above range — Patterns on the Diabetes tab shows which meals or times of day push you high.

reason: time in range down on last week
title: Time in range down {dx_tir_delta} points
body: Down on last week. Illness, stress, less activity or a change in eating are the usual causes — worth a look at the weekly health check on the Diabetes tab.

title: Glucose swings: variability {dx_cv_7d}%
body: Above the 36% target — big swings, not just the average, drive lows and how you feel. Pre-bolusing 10-15 min before carbs and splitting doses for high-fat meals are the usual fixes.

title: Sensor data patchy ({dx_coverage_24h}% of readings)
body: Gaps make the stats and forecasts less reliable. Check the sensor, phone Bluetooth and the uploader.

title: Time in range up {dx_tir_delta} points
body: Better than last week — whatever changed is working. {dx_tir_7d}% in range now.

title: Excellent week: {dx_tir_7d}% in range
body: Above the 70% target with lows under control. Estimated HbA1c (GMI) about {dx_gmi:1}%.

title: {dx_tir_24h}% in range over 24h
body: A really steady day.

title: Estimated HbA1c about {dx_gmi:1}%
body: GMI from your last 7 days of CGM (average {dx_mean_7d:1} mmol/L). Time in range {dx_tir_7d}%.

headline: Recovery {recovery}
action: Take it easy — light walk today
title: Recovery {recovery} — take it easy
body: Well below your normal. Rest or active recovery only: a walk, mobility, an easy spin. Keep strain under 8 and get to bed early.

headline: Recovery {recovery}, but you felt rough
action: Keep it moderate today
title: Numbers say go, you say no
body: Recovery is {recovery} but you feel rough. Trust the feeling today — keep it moderate. Your check-ins teach Recovery what matters for you.

headline: Recovery {recovery}, but you feel good
action: A moderate session is fine — stop early if your heart rate runs high
title: You feel better than your numbers
body: Recovery {recovery} but you feel good. A moderate session is reasonable — stop early if heart rate runs higher than usual for the effort.

headline: Recovery {recovery}
action: Train, but go lighter — technique work, fewer hard sets
title: Recovery {recovery} — go lighter
body: Below your normal. Train, but cap the intensity: technique work, fewer hard sets, strain {strain_target_lo:1}-{strain_target_hi:1}.

headline: You've recovered well ({recovery})
action: Push hard today
title: Green light — Recovery {recovery}
body: Well recovered. A good day for your hardest session or a PB attempt — strain target {strain_target_lo:1}-{strain_target_hi:1}.

headline: Recovery {recovery}, about your normal
action: Train as planned — strain {strain_target_lo:1}-{strain_target_hi:1}
title: Recovery {recovery} — train as planned
body: Around your normal. Stick to the plan; strain target {strain_target_lo:1}-{strain_target_hi:1}.

action: Plan a deload or two easy days
title: HRV down all week
body: Your 7-day HRV average is well below your normal — the most reliable sign of accumulated fatigue. Plan a deload or two easy days, and protect sleep.

action: Pick a fixed bedtime for the next 3 nights
title: {short_nights_7} short nights this week
body: Four or more nights under 6 hours affects recovery, appetite, mood and glucose control more than any single bad night. Pick a fixed bedtime for the next 3 nights.

action: Ease off for a couple of days
title: Resting heart rate creeping up
body: Up on your normal all week. Common causes: hard training without enough rest, poor sleep, alcohol, stress or an illness coming on. Ease off for a couple of days.

title: HRV trending up
body: Your 7-day HRV average is above your normal — you're adapting well to your training. A good week to progress.

headline: Only {sleep_hrs:1}h sleep
action: Skip max-effort lifts and aim for {sleep_need:1}h tonight
title: Only {sleep_hrs:1}h sleep
body: Reaction time, appetite control and glucose all suffer after a night under 5 hours. Skip max-effort lifts, get daylight early, keep caffeine before noon, and aim for {sleep_need:1}h tonight.

action: Go to bed 30-45 min earlier for three nights
title: Sleep debt building ({sleep_debt:1}h)
body: Going to bed 30-45 minutes earlier for three nights clears most of it — more effective than one long lie-in.

title: High glucose and poor sleep
body: Running high overnight (average {dx_night_mean:1}) disturbs sleep, and poor sleep raises insulin resistance the next day. Fixing the overnight highs often improves both.

headline: Short night: {sleep_hrs:1}h
action: Keep training moderate today
title: Short night: {sleep_hrs:1}h
body: Below what you need. Keep today's training moderate and aim for {sleep_need:1}h tonight.

title: Sleep target met
body: {sleep_hrs:1}h — {sleep_perf}% of what you needed. Nights like this are what make the rest of the plan work.

action: No hard training — make it an early night
title: Body Battery {battery}% — empty
body: Running on fumes. Drop anything optional, no hard training, eat a proper meal and make tonight an early night.

action: Keep the rest of the evening light
title: Body Battery {battery}% — very low
body: Keep the rest of the day light: a short walk outside, a proper meal, screens down early. Anything hard now will cost you tomorrow.

title: Only charged +{battery_charged}% overnight
body: A weak recharge usually comes from short sleep, alcohol, a late heavy meal, hard training close to bed, or a night low. Woke on {battery_wake}%.

action: Plan a lighter day
title: Woke on {battery_wake}%
body: You didn't recharge fully. Plan a lighter day and protect tonight's sleep.

title: Stress, not training, is draining you
body: −{battery_stress_drain}% today from raised heart rate while not exercising. Short walks, a 5-minute slow-breathing break (about 6 breaths a minute) and caffeine before noon only help most.

title: Draining fast ({battery_rate:1}%/hr)
body: Stress or activity is high right now. If you're not training, a few minutes of slow breathing is the quickest way to bring it down.

title: On course for 25% by about {battery_low_hour}:00
body: At this rate you'll be very low by early evening. Pace the afternoon: a calm break or a short walk outside slows the drain.

title: Low battery for a workout ({battery}%)
body: If you train today, keep it short and easy — 20-30 minutes of easy cardio or technique work rather than heavy lifting.

action: Wind down early — screens off 30 min before bed
title: Wind down early ({battery}%)
body: Dim lights, screens off 30 minutes before bed, and aim for {sleep_need:1}h — a good night is the only real recharge.

title: Charged up, but Recovery is low
body: Body Battery {battery}% but Recovery {recovery}. Energy for the day is fine; the low Recovery says your body is still absorbing recent training — avoid max efforts.

title: Woke on {battery_wake}%
body: Fully recharged (+{battery_charged}% overnight). A great day for your hardest session.

title: Great recharge: +{battery_charged}%
body: A strong night — whatever you did yesterday evening, repeat it.

title: Plenty in the tank ({battery}%)
body: Body Battery and Recovery both support a proper session today.

action: A short walk now helps you fall asleep
title: Still on {battery}% this evening
body: A quiet day. A short walk now builds sleep pressure — you'll fall asleep faster.

title: Recharging (+{battery_rate:1}%/hr)
body: Calm rest is topping you up. Nice.

reason: strain {strain:1}, over target on a low-recovery day
action: Refuel with protein and carbs, then an early night
title: Past today's strain target
body: Strain {strain:1} against a target of {strain_target_lo:1}-{strain_target_hi:1} on a low-recovery day. Stop here: refuel with protein and carbs and get to bed early.

action: Prioritise protein, fluids and sleep
title: Big day yesterday (strain {strain_yday:1})
body: Expect Recovery to dip. Prioritise protein (about 30-40g a meal), fluids and sleep today.

reason: strain only {strain:1} on a green day
action: A 30-min brisk walk would use it well
title: Room left today
body: Green recovery but strain only {strain:1}. A 30-minute brisk walk or short session would use it well.

reason: {workouts_7d} sessions in 7 days with HRV dipping
action: Take a full rest day in the next two days
title: {workouts_7d} sessions in 7 days, HRV dipping
body: Training volume is outpacing recovery. Schedule a full rest day in the next two days.

action: Get back in, even a short session
title: {days_since_workout} days since your last workout
body: Recovery is good — a good day to get back in, even a short session keeps the habit going.

action: Have a protein-rich meal this evening
title: Only {consumed} of {eat_target} kcal so far
body: A very big deficit hurts sleep and recovery and makes tomorrow's hunger worse. Have a protein-rich meal this evening.

action: Add 200-300 kcal on training days
title: Big deficit this week: {weekly_net_abs} kcal
body: About {weekly_kg:1}kg of fat — losing faster than roughly 1% of bodyweight a week risks muscle. Add 200-300 kcal on training days, mostly protein and carbs.

title: Surplus this week: +{weekly_net} kcal
body: Eating more than you've burned over 7 days, which works against your weight plan. Logging every meal for the next few days is the quickest way to see where it's coming from.

title: {over_kcal} kcal over today's target
body: Fine now and then — it's the weekly total that counts. Keep tomorrow at target.

title: Nothing logged yet today
body: Log what you've eaten so far — same-day logging is far more accurate than remembering tonight.

reason: a steady {weekly_net_abs} kcal deficit this week
title: Steady deficit: {weekly_net_abs} kcal this week
body: About {weekly_kg:1}kg of fat a week — a sustainable pace that protects muscle.

action: Keep protein high and keep lifting
title: Down {weight_change_14d:1}kg in two weeks
body: Faster than ideal for keeping muscle. Keep protein high (about 1.6-2g per kg) and keep lifting; consider eating a little more on training days.

reason: weight flat for two weeks despite a deficit
action: Give it another week before changing anything
title: Weight flat for two weeks
body: Despite a deficit — usually water retention (new training, salt, stress, poor sleep) masking fat loss, or meals missing from the log. Give it another week before changing anything.

action: A 20-min walk after dinner
title: {steps} steps — {steps_left} to go
body: A 20-minute walk after dinner is about 2,000 steps, and it blunts the post-meal glucose rise too.

title: Step goal hit: {steps}
body: Nice work.
